لَهِيدٌ A beast of carriage jaded, or fatigued, (S, L,) and rendered emaciated, or lean, by being ridden. (L.) ―
-b2- A she-camel pressed, or squeezed, and having her flesh bruised, by her load. (Lh, L.) ―
-b3- لَهِيدٌ and ↓ مَلْهُودٌ A camel oppressed by the weight of a load, and squeezed: having his back or side squeezed by a heavy load, or bruised so that it is swollen, and galled: having his side squeezed by a heavy load so that a disease has been the consequence, which has disordered his lungs. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
